Proposition

1. ch4:4.46Suppose $E$ and $M$ are nonempty connected smooth manifolds with or without boundary. A proper local diffeomorphism $\pi :E o M$ is a smooth covering map.

Proof

\sketch The local diffeomorphism $\pi $ is open and properness makes it closed, so its nonempty image is both open and closed in connected $M$; hence $\pi $ is surjective. For $q\in M$, the fiber $\pi ^{-1}(q)$ is discrete by local injectivity and compact by properness, hence finite, say $\{ p_1,\ldots ,p_k\} $. Choose pairwise disjoint neighborhoods $V_i$ on which $\pi $ is a diffeomorphism onto open $U_i i q$, and set $U= igcap _iU_i$. With

\[ K=E\setminus (V_1\cup \cdots \cup V_k), \]

Since $q otin \pi (K)$, replace $U$ by $U\setminus \pi (K)$ and then by its connected component containing $q$. Then

egin{equation} U\subseteq U_i\quad ext{for every }i, ag {4.8} \end{equation}

and

egin{equation} \pi ^{-1}(U)\subseteq V_1\cup \cdots \cup V_k. ag {4.9} \end{equation}

The sets $\widetilde V_i=\pi ^{-1}(U)\cap V_i$ are disjoint, connected, open, cover $\pi ^{-1}(U)$, and each maps diffeomorphically onto $U$. They are therefore exactly its components, so $U$ is evenly covered.

□
